Nestle (VTX:NESN) has been assigned a CHF 97 target price by investment analysts at JPMorgan Chase in a research note issued to investors on Monday. The firm presently has a “buy” rating on the stock. JPMorgan Chase’s price target suggests a potential upside of 26.80% from the stock’s previous close.
Several other brokerages also recently commented on NESN. Goldman Sachs set a CHF 96 target price on Nestle and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Wednesday, May 2nd. UBS set a CHF 80 target price on Nestle and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research note on Thursday, April 19th. Royal Bank of Canada set a CHF 82 target price on Nestle and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Monday, March 26th. Barclays set a CHF 83 target price on Nestle and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research note on Tuesday, April 24th. Finally, BNP Paribas set a CHF 74 target price on Nestle and gave the stock a “sell” rating in a research note on Tuesday, April 17th. Two investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seven have assigned a hold rating and eleven have issued a buy rating to the stock. Nestle has an average rating of “Hold” and an average target price of CHF 86.22.

NESN opened at CHF 76.50 on Monday. Nestle has a twelve month low of CHF 73.34 and a twelve month high of CHF 86.40.
Nestle Company Profile
Nestle SA is a nutrition, health and wellness company. The Company’s segments are Zone Europe, Middle East and North Africa (EMENA); Zone Americas (AMS); Zone Asia, Oceania and sub-Saharan Africa (AOA); Nestle Waters; Nestle Nutrition, and Other Businesses. The Company operates in the United States, Greater China Region, Switzerland and Rest of the World. This entry was posted in stocks on by admin .
